pi0.description: π0 is a general-purpose robot foundation model released by Physical Intelligence. Its architecture of a VLM plus a flow matching action expert achieves 50Hz continuous control, and since being open-sourced it has become one of the most commonly used VLA fine-tuning bases in academia and industry.
highlights: The first general-purpose VLA to validate flow matching action generation at scale
Open-sourced weights and fine-tuning code, with an active community ecosystem
A benchmark performer on long-horizon dexterous manipulation (such as folding clothes)
High-frequency continuous control with smooth motion

specs.architecture: VLM backbone + action expert (flow matching)
specs.training_data: Large-scale in-house data from 7 robots across 68 task types + open-source data
specs.embodiments: Single-arm / bimanual robot arms, mobile manipulation platforms and other embodiments
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; pre-training covers multiple embodiments and can be fine-tuned for transfer
specs.benchmark_note: Significantly ahead of contemporaneous baselines on long-horizon dexterous tasks such as folding clothes and clearing tables
specs.deploy_note: Inference on a single consumer-grade GPU; the official openpi provides a fine-tuning workflow

nvidia-cosmos.description: Cosmos is NVIDIA's world foundation model platform for physical AI. Trained on approx. 20 million hours of video, it offers both diffusion and autoregressive models, is widely used for robot data synthesis and policy evaluation, and is currently the most mainstream open-source world model family.
highlights: An open-source, commercially usable family of world foundation models with a complete ecosystem
Deeply integrated with the Isaac/Omniverse simulation pipeline
Supports generation from text, image and video conditions
Specifically optimized for physical consistency in physical AI scenarios

specs.architecture: Video world foundation models with two technical routes: diffusion + autoregressive
specs.action_conditioned: Supports action/trajectory conditioned control (Cosmos Transfer/Reason series extensions)
specs.training_data: Approx. 20 million hours of real-world video
specs.use_case: Robot/autonomous driving synthetic data generation, policy evaluation, simulation augmentation
specs.benchmark_note: Physical consistency is in the top tier among open-source world models

rt-2.description: RT-2 is a vision-language-action model proposed by Google DeepMind in 2023. It represents actions as text tokens and is co-trained with internet image-text data, giving robots semantic reasoning and generalization. It is the pioneering work of the VLA paradigm, but is not open source.
highlights: First to propose and validate the vision-language-action (VLA) paradigm
Transfers web knowledge to robot control, with semantic reasoning ability
Generalizes markedly better than RT-1 on unseen objects and instructions
Spawned follow-up work such as OpenVLA

specs.architecture: Vision-language model directly outputs action tokens (actions discretized as text)
specs.training_data: Co-trained on internet image-text data + Everyday Robots demonstration data
specs.embodiments: Everyday Robots mobile manipulator arm
specs.cross_embodiment: Not a focus of validation in the paper
specs.benchmark_note: Generalization success rate on unseen objects, backgrounds and instructions is approx. twice that of RT-1
specs.deploy_note: The large model relies on cloud TPU inference, with a low control frequency

openvla.description: OpenVLA is an open-source 7B VLA model jointly released by Stanford, Berkeley and Toyota Research Institute, among others. Based on Llama 2 and trained on Open X-Embodiment data, it outperforms the 55B RT-2-X, supports low-cost fine-tuning, and is a commonly used community baseline.
highlights: The first open-source 7B general-purpose VLA model
Only about 1/7 the parameters of RT-2-X yet performs better
Supports LoRA and quantization, and can be fine-tuned on consumer GPUs
One of the VLAs most widely reproduced and built upon by the community

specs.architecture: VLA with a vision encoder + Llama 2 language model
specs.training_data: Approx. 970,000 robot trajectories from the Open X-Embodiment dataset
specs.embodiments: Mainly robot arms such as WidowX and Google Robot; can be fine-tuned to adapt to new embodiments
specs.cross_embodiment: Supported; can adapt to new embodiments via LoRA fine-tuning
specs.benchmark_note: The paper reports a success rate approx. 16.5 percentage points higher than the 55B RT-2-X, with only about 1/7 of its parameters
specs.deploy_note: Approx. 6Hz on an RTX 4090; supports quantization and LoRA fine-tuning

pi05.description: π0.5 is a VLA model from Physical Intelligence built on π0. Through co-training on multi-source data and high-level subtask prediction, it lets robots complete long-horizon tidying tasks in real homes never seen during training; its weights were later released via openpi.
highlights: Emphasizes open-world generalization, performing tasks in brand-new home environments
Predicts a high-level subtask first and then outputs actions, making long-horizon tasks more robust
Co-trained on multi-source data to improve semantic understanding
Weights released through openpi

specs.architecture: Hierarchical reasoning + action expert, supporting high-level subtask prediction
specs.training_data: Co-trained on multiple robot datasets, internet vision-language data and high-level semantic annotation data
specs.embodiments: Mobile manipulation robots, bimanual robots and other embodiments
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong, with emphasis on open-world generalization in unseen home environments
specs.benchmark_note: Can complete long-horizon tasks such as tidying kitchens and bedrooms in real homes absent from training
specs.deploy_note: Requires a higher-end GPU for inference; openpi provides a fine-tuning workflow

octo.description: Octo is an open-source general-purpose robot policy released by Berkeley, Stanford and Carnegie Mellon, among others. With only approx. 93 million parameters, it is pre-trained on Open X-Embodiment data with a diffusion action head and can be quickly fine-tuned to new robot embodiments, making it suitable for low-compute scenarios.
highlights: Lightweight general-purpose robot policy with only 27M to 93M parameters
Supports both language and goal image task specification
Low cost and fast fine-tuning to new embodiments
Fully open source, including training code and weights

specs.architecture: Transformer policy with a diffusion action head
specs.training_data: Approx. 800,000 robot trajectories from Open X-Embodiment
specs.embodiments: Pre-training data from 9 robot platforms; can be fine-tuned to new embodiments
specs.cross_embodiment: Supported; makes it easy to quickly fine-tune to new sensors and action spaces
specs.benchmark_note: Outperformed the open-source baselines of the time in zero-shot and fine-tuned performance across multiple robots
specs.deploy_note: The model is very small and can be fine-tuned and run on consumer-grade GPUs

rdt-1b.description: RDT-1B is a bimanual manipulation diffusion foundation model with approx. 1.2 billion parameters released by a Tsinghua University team. Based on a Diffusion Transformer with a unified action space, it is pre-trained on multi-robot data, has strong few-shot ability, and its weights and code are open source.
highlights: One of the largest diffusion foundation models for bimanual manipulation, with approx. 1.2 billion parameters
A unified action space designed for bimanual coordinated manipulation
Strong few-shot and zero-shot generalization
Tsinghua open-sourced the weights and training code

specs.architecture: Diffusion Transformer foundation model
specs.backbone: Language encoder T5-XXL + vision encoder SigLIP
specs.training_data: Pre-trained on multi-robot datasets, and fine-tuned on in-house collected ALOHA bimanual data
specs.embodiments: Mainly ALOHA bimanual robots
specs.cross_embodiment: Proposes a unified action space to merge multi-embodiment data
specs.benchmark_note: Outperforms baselines such as Octo and OpenVLA on real bimanual tasks, with few-shot ability
specs.deploy_note: Pre-training and fine-tuning code provided; training requires large GPU memory

nvidia-gr00t-n1.description: GR00T N1 is an open humanoid robot foundation model released by NVIDIA in 2025, with approx. 2.2 billion parameters. It uses a dual-system architecture of a vision-language module plus a diffusion Transformer action module, is trained on a mix of real, video and synthetic data, and can be adapted to different robots through post-training.
highlights: One of the world's first open foundation models for general-purpose humanoid robots
Dual-system architecture balancing language understanding and high-frequency action
Trained on a mix of real, video and synthetic data
Forms a data loop together with Isaac Lab and Cosmos

specs.architecture: Dual system: vision-language module (slow thinking) + diffusion Transformer action module (fast execution)
specs.training_data: Mix of real robot trajectories, human videos and synthetic simulation data
specs.embodiments: Targets humanoid robots, and also adapts to various robot arms
specs.cross_embodiment: Supported; can adapt to different embodiments via post-training
specs.benchmark_note: Outperforms imitation learning baselines on simulation benchmarks and real humanoid tasks
specs.deploy_note: Post-training workflow provided; deployed with the Isaac and Jetson platforms

figure-helix.description: Helix is a humanoid robot VLA released by Figure AI in 2025. It combines an approx. 7B slow language-vision system with an approx. 80M, 200Hz fast control policy, can control the entire upper body and supports two-robot collaboration. It runs on an onboard GPU and is not open source.
highlights: The first VLA to control a humanoid's entire upper body, including the fingers
Dual-system design balancing semantic understanding and 200Hz high-frequency control
Supports multi-robot collaboration, demonstrated with two robots tidying items together
Runs entirely on an onboard embedded GPU

specs.architecture: Dual system: slow VLM (System 2) + fast visuomotor policy (System 1)
specs.action_head: Approx. 80M-parameter fast policy outputs continuous actions
specs.training_data: Approx. 500 hours of multi-robot, multi-operator teleoperation data
specs.embodiments: Figure humanoid robot (35 DOF in the upper body)
specs.cross_embodiment: Mainly targets Figure's own embodiment
specs.benchmark_note: Demonstrated two robots collaboratively putting away groceries and other tasks, and can grasp arbitrary household items zero-shot
specs.deploy_note: Runs on an onboard low-power GPU

gemini-robotics.description: Gemini Robotics is a VLA model launched by Google DeepMind in 2025 based on Gemini 2.0. It can directly control robots to perform dexterous tasks such as folding origami and zipping zippers. The family also includes an embodied reasoning model, and it is developed with partners such as Apptronik, but the model is not open source.
highlights: A multimodal robot foundation model based on Gemini 2.0
Stronger language understanding and generalization
Supports highly dexterous tasks such as folding origami and zipping zippers
Later followed by an On-Device version that runs locally

specs.architecture: VLA based on Gemini 2.0, plus an embodied reasoning version, Gemini Robotics-ER
specs.action_head: Continuous action output (cloud model + on-device action decoding)
specs.training_data: Large-scale robot teleoperation data + multimodal internet data
specs.embodiments: ALOHA 2 bimanual, Apptronik Apollo humanoid, etc.
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; can adapt to different robot configurations
specs.benchmark_note: Showed strong generalization and language understanding on dexterous tasks such as folding paper and zipping zippers
specs.deploy_note: An On-Device version that runs locally on the robot was also released

agibot-go-1.description: GO-1 is a general-purpose embodied foundation model released by AgiBot in 2025. It uses the ViLLA architecture, composed of a latent action planner and an action expert, is trained on AgiBot World's million-scale real trajectories, comes with an open dataset, and is used for AgiBot's robot series.
highlights: Proposes the ViLLA architecture, introducing latent action representations
Trained on AgiBot World's million-scale real trajectories
Dataset and part of the code are publicly available
Paired with AgiBot Genie G1 and the Expedition series

specs.architecture: ViLLA (Vision-Language-Latent-Action): latent action planner + action expert
specs.backbone: Vision-language model backbone + latent action planning
specs.training_data: AgiBot World dataset (over 1 million real robot trajectories)
specs.embodiments: AgiBot Genie G1 and others
specs.cross_embodiment: Claimed to transfer to different embodiments
specs.benchmark_note: The official report shows a clear improvement in success rate on complex tasks over previous open-source baselines
specs.deploy_note: Paired with the AgiBot World dataset and development platform

smolvla.description: SmolVLA is a lightweight open-source VLA released by Hugging Face in 2025, with only approx. 450 million parameters. Based on SmolVLM and a flow matching action expert, it is trained entirely on publicly available community data, runs on consumer-grade hardware, and targets LeRobot low-cost robot arms.
highlights: A lightweight VLA with only approx. 450 million parameters
Trained entirely on publicly available community data, open and transparent
Can be trained and run on a consumer GPU or laptop
Deeply integrated with the LeRobot low-cost robot arm ecosystem

specs.architecture: Lightweight VLM + action expert
specs.training_data: Public robot datasets from the LeRobot community (approx. 23,000 trajectories)
specs.embodiments: Low-cost robot arms such as SO-100 / SO-101
specs.cross_embodiment: Mainly targets low-cost desktop robot arms
specs.benchmark_note: Comparable to larger models on simulated and real tasks
specs.deploy_note: Runs on consumer GPUs and even a MacBook; supports asynchronous inference

google-genie-2.description: Genie 2 is a foundation world model released by Google DeepMind in late 2024. It can generate an interactive 3D environment from a single image, supports keyboard and mouse action control, and maintains temporal consistency for about a minute. It is mainly used to provide training environments for AI agents and is not open source.
highlights: Generates an interactive 3D world from a single image
Supports keyboard and mouse action control while maintaining some temporal consistency
Can provide unlimited training environments for agents such as SIMA
Demonstrated emergent physics, lighting and reflections

specs.architecture: Autoregressive latent-space diffusion world model
specs.modality: Generates interactive 3D environment video from a single image
specs.horizon: Typically tens of seconds, up to approx. 1 minute
specs.action_conditioned: Supports real-time control via keyboard/mouse action input
specs.training_data: Large-scale video dataset
specs.use_case: Generating open-ended training environments for AI agents
specs.benchmark_note: Demonstrated long-term consistency in object interaction, lighting and physics

wayve-gaia-2.description: GAIA-2 is a generative world model for autonomous driving released by Wayve of the UK. It can generate multi-camera consistent driving video and supports controlling conditions such as ego-vehicle actions, traffic participants and weather. It is used to synthesize long-tail scenarios and evaluate driving policies, and is not open source.
highlights: Multi-camera consistent driving video generation
Can control ego-vehicle actions and the behavior of traffic participants
Supports editing conditions such as weather, lighting and road type
Used to generate rare safety-critical scenarios

specs.architecture: Latent-space diffusion world model
specs.action_conditioned: Supports control of ego-vehicle actions, other traffic participants and environmental conditions
specs.training_data: Real driving data from multiple countries including the UK, US and Germany
specs.use_case: Autonomous driving scenario synthesis and long-tail scenario simulation
specs.benchmark_note: Can generate multi-camera consistent driving scenes and supports conditions such as weather and time of day

1x-world-model.description: The 1X World Model is an action-conditioned video world model trained by 1X Technologies on real data from its own humanoid robots. It can predict the visual outcome after a robot action, is used for policy evaluation and iteration to reduce real-robot testing costs, and serves the NEO home robot.
highlights: Trained on data collected from real robots, closely matching its own embodiment
Policies can be evaluated inside the world model, reducing real-robot testing
Action-conditioned prediction, simulating the consequences of interactions
Supports iteration of the NEO home robot

specs.architecture: Action-conditioned world model based on video generation
specs.action_conditioned: Generates future video conditioned on robot actions
specs.training_data: Large-scale data collected by 1X humanoid robots in real homes and offices
specs.use_case: Evaluating robot policies, replacing part of real-world testing
specs.benchmark_note: Officially shown to correlate highly with real-world policy performance

unisim.description: UniSim is a universal interactive world simulator proposed in 2023 by Google DeepMind together with Berkeley and others. It uses a video diffusion model to generate subsequent frames from text or actions, lets policies be trained within it and transferred to real robots, and established the idea of world models as simulators.
highlights: Among the first to propose using a video generation model as a universal interactive simulator
Unifies multiple data sources, covering robots, human activity and simulation
Supports two levels of conditioning: high-level instructions and low-level control
Selected as an Outstanding Paper at ICLR 2024

specs.architecture: Action-conditioned video diffusion model
specs.modality: Video generation conditioned on text or low-level actions
specs.action_conditioned: Supports high-level text instructions and low-level motion control
specs.training_data: Multi-source data: simulation renderings, real robots, human activity videos and image-text data
specs.use_case: Interactive simulation for training policies, long-horizon planning and vision-language models
specs.benchmark_note: Policies trained within it transfer to real robots, validating the feasibility of world models as simulators

nvidia-gr00t-n1-7.description: NVIDIA Isaac GR00T N1.7 is an open 3B humanoid VLA model released by NVIDIA in 2026. Combining a Cosmos-Reason2-2B VLM backbone with a flow-matching action head and 20K hours of human video pre-training, it runs at ~28 Hz on Jetson Thor and is commercially usable.
highlights: 3B open humanoid foundation model for commercial use, reaching GA in Nov 2026
Pre-trained with 20K hours of EgoScale human video for stronger instruction following
Achieves ~28 Hz edge inference on Jetson AGX Thor
Full LeRobot dataset format and post-training workflow support

specs.architecture: Dual system: VLM backbone (Cosmos-Reason2-2B) + flow-matching diffusion action head
specs.training_data: Bimanual, semi-humanoid, expansive humanoid data + 20K hours EgoScale human video
specs.embodiments: General humanoid robots and bimanual manipulators
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; supports fine-tuning transfer in LeRobot format
specs.benchmark_note: With TensorRT: ~40 Hz on RTX PRO 6000, ~35.9 Hz on H100, ~28 Hz on Jetson AGX Thor
specs.deploy_note: Requires ≥16 GB VRAM for inference; ≥40 GB VRAM recommended for fine-tuning

molmoact2.description: MolmoAct2 is a fully open VLA model released by Ai2 in May 2026. It grafts a flow-matching continuous-action expert onto the Molmo2-ER embodied-reasoning VLM via per-layer KV conditioning, open-sourcing weights, code, 720 hours of bimanual YAM data, and OpenFAST Tokenizer while outperforming π0.5.
highlights: Fully open weights, training code, 720-hour bimanual dataset and tokenizer
Built on Molmo2-ER, leading across 13 embodied-reasoning benchmarks
Zero-shot out-of-the-box deployment on DROID and SO-100/101
MolmoAct2-Think adaptive depth variant lowers inference latency
applications: Zero-shot deployment on low-cost robot arms
Embodied spatial reasoning and open research

specs.architecture: Molmo2-ER autoregressive VLM + per-layer KV-conditioned flow-matching action expert
specs.training_data: 720h bimanual YAM + DROID + SO-100/101 + multimodal web and reasoning data
specs.embodiments: Franka DROID, bimanual YAM, SO-100/101, etc.
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; DROID and SO-100/101 checkpoints deploy zero-shot out of the box
specs.benchmark_note: Significantly outperforms π0.5 on LIBERO, RoboEval and 8 real-world bimanual tasks
specs.deploy_note: Offers MolmoAct2-Think adaptive-depth reasoning variant for lower latency

nvidia-cosmos-3.description: NVIDIA Cosmos 3 is an omnimodal Physical AI world foundation model released in June 2026. It unifies language reasoning, video world simulation and robot action tokens in one framework, with open weights in 16B Nano and 64B Super sizes.
highlights: Unifies VLM, video world simulator and world-action model (WAM) in a single architecture
Open weights available in 16B Nano and 64B Super sizes
Released under Linux Foundation OpenMDW-1.1 license with datasets and benchmarks
Closes the Physical AI loop across synthetic data generation and policy evaluation
applications: Embodied AI and autonomous driving simulation

specs.architecture: Omnimodal world foundation model unifying understanding, world generation and action tokens
specs.modality: Text, image, video, audio and robot actions
specs.action_conditioned: Treats action as a core modality, outputting physically grounded control signals
specs.training_data: Large-scale real and synthetic Physical AI multimodal data
specs.use_case: Generalist embodied policies (WAM), synthetic training data and physics simulation
specs.benchmark_note: Available in 16B Nano and 64B Super; ranked #1 open policy model on RoboArena at report release

google-genie-3.description: Genie 3 is a real-time interactive world model launched by Google DeepMind in 2026. Using a latent action model, it is the first to generate persistent, physically coherent explorable 3D environments at 24 fps in real time, available as a closed API.
highlights: Breaks through to 24 fps real-time generation for truly interactive exploration
Generated 3D environments maintain stronger spatial and temporal persistence
Learns a compressed latent action space from video without labeled actions
Provides high-fidelity online interactive environments for generalist AI agents

specs.architecture: Latent action model + real-time interactive 3D world generation
specs.action_conditioned: Supports real-time user and agent action control with physical coherence
specs.training_data: Large-scale unlabeled video data
specs.use_case: Real-time interactive agent training and embodied environment simulation
specs.benchmark_note: First world model to generate persistent interactive 3D environments at 24 fps in real time

openvla-oft.description: OpenVLA-OFT (Optimized Fine-Tuning) upgrades OpenVLA with parallel decoding, action chunking, and continuous L1 regression, lifting average success on four LIBERO suites from 76.5% to 97.1% with 26x higher action throughput and beating fine-tuned π0 and RDT-1B on bimanual ALOHA.
highlights: Replaces autoregressive discrete tokens with parallel decoding and continuous action chunking
Boosts OpenVLA's LIBERO average success rate from 76.5% to 97.1%
Increases action generation throughput by 26x for smoother real-robot control
Outperforms fine-tuned π0 and RDT-1B by up to 15% absolute on bimanual ALOHA tasks

specs.architecture: VLM backbone + parallel decoding, action chunking & continuous L1 regression
specs.training_data: Optimized fine-tuning recipe on OpenVLA pretraining for bimanual & tabletop tasks
specs.embodiments: Single-arm and bimanual ALOHA manipulators
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; adapts rapidly via OFT recipe to bimanual platforms
specs.benchmark_note: 97.1% avg on LIBERO (vs 76.5% OpenVLA); up to +15% over π0/RDT-1B on ALOHA
specs.deploy_note: 26x higher throughput than OpenVLA; open-source code and pretrained checkpoints

wall-oss-0-5.description: Wall-OSS-0.5 is an open-source 4B VLA model from X Square Robot built on Qwen2.5-VL-3B and a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone, achieving 15 Hz high-resolution inference and zero-shot real-robot execution across a 17-task suite via gradient-bridged pretraining.
highlights: Open-source 4B VLA built on a 3B Qwen2.5-VL backbone with MoT routing
Gradient-bridged co-training unifies multimodal CE, action-token CE and flow matching
Deployment-oriented pretraining evaluated zero-shot across 17 real-robot tasks
15 Hz high-res inference supported by the open-source Wall-X 1.1.0 runtime

specs.architecture: Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) routing backbone + gradient-bridged co-training
specs.action_head: Flow Matching continuous actions + Vision-Aligned RVQ Action Tokenizer
specs.training_data: Self-collected manipulation data + open multi-embodiment datasets + multimodal corpora
specs.embodiments: Single-arm, bimanual and mobile manipulation platforms
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; focused on deployment-oriented zero-shot pretraining
specs.benchmark_note: Evaluated directly on a 17-task real-robot zero-shot suite prior to task fine-tuning
specs.deploy_note: 15 Hz inference at high input resolution; Wall-X 1.1.0 runtime & DMuon support

lingbot-vla.description: LingBot-VLA is an open-source pragmatic VLA foundation model from Robbyant (Ant Group), pre-trained on ~20,000 hours of real-world data across 9 bimanual configurations and delivering 261 samples/s/GPU training throughput.
highlights: Pre-trained on ~20,000 hours of real-world data from 9 popular dual-arm configurations
Outperforms baselines across 3 robot platforms × 100 tasks (130 episodes/task)
Efficient codebase achieves 261 samples/s/GPU on 8-GPU setups (1.5–2.8x speedup)
Open access to code, base model and benchmarks; paired with LingBot-Touch ecosystem

specs.architecture: Pragmatic industrial VLA foundation model with high-throughput distributed training
specs.training_data: ~20,000 hours of real-world data across 9 dual-arm robot configurations
specs.embodiments: 9 dual-arm robot configurations
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; validated across 3 embodiments × 100 tasks
specs.benchmark_note: Combining with LingBot-Touch adds +13.9% mean success on 26 dexterous hand tasks
specs.deploy_note: 261 samples/s/GPU training throughput (1.5–2.8x faster than existing VLA codebases)

v-jepa-2.description: V-JEPA 2 is Meta FAIR's open-weights self-supervised video world model predicting physical dynamics in latent space. Post-trained on <62 hours of DROID video, its action-conditioned V-JEPA 2-AC plans zero-shot pick-and-place on Franka arms from image goals.
highlights: Flagship JEPA world model predicting world dynamics in latent space rather than pixels
Lightweight 0.3B open-weights base model with high representation efficiency
V-JEPA 2-AC post-trains on <62 h DROID video for zero-shot Franka pick-and-place
V-JEPA 2.1 adds +20 points on real-robot grasping over V-JEPA 2-AC

specs.architecture: Self-supervised Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) + action-conditioned (AC)
specs.modality: Latent physical representation prediction & action-conditioned planning
specs.horizon: Multi-step action planning conditioned on image goals
specs.action_conditioned: V-JEPA 2-AC post-trained on <62h DROID video for zero-shot Franka manipulation
specs.training_data: Large-scale self-supervised video + <62h DROID action video
specs.use_case: Pixel-free physical understanding, zero-shot grasping and action planning
specs.benchmark_note: V-JEPA 2.1 improves real-robot grasping by +20 points over V-JEPA 2-AC

world-labs-marble.description: World Labs Marble, launched in Nov 2025, is World Labs' first commercial multimodal world model. It turns text, images, panoramas or video into persistent, explorable 3D worlds exportable as Gaussian splats or meshes, with a developer World API opened in Jan 2026.
highlights: First commercial multimodal spatial world model from Fei-Fei Li's World Labs
Generates persistent 3D environments exportable as Gaussian splats and meshes (unlike 2D video)
Converts text, photos, panoramas or video into navigable 3D scenes for Unreal & simulation
Developer World API opened in Jan 2026 alongside Marble 1.1 / 1.1 Plus iterations
applications: High-fidelity 3D scene asset generation for robotics

specs.architecture: Multimodal spatial intelligence 3D world generation model
specs.action_conditioned: Supports interactive camera exploration, editing & Unreal pipeline export
specs.training_data: Large-scale multimodal spatial & 3D data
specs.use_case: Persistent 3D simulation environment generation and spatial intelligence
specs.benchmark_note: Publicly launched Nov 2025; World API opened Jan 2026; iterated to Marble 1.1 Plus

ace-kaiwu-3.description: Kaiwu World Model 3.0-4B (Kairos 3.0 / 3.1) from ACE Robotics is an open-source, commercially deployed 4B embodied world model supporting up to 7-minute video generation, force-mechanics input, and Puffin 3D camera perception, ranking #1 on WorldModelBench Robot (9.30), LIBERO-Plus (89.0), and RoboTwin 2.0 (96.1%).
highlights: Developed by ACE Robotics (led by SenseTime co-founder Xiaogang Wang); compact 4B parameters supporting 7-minute video generation (evolved to Kairos 3.1)
Ranked #1 globally on WorldModelBench Robot (9.30, beating 28B LingBot & 16B Cosmos 3), LIBERO-Plus (89.0), RoboTwin 2.0 (96.1%), and DreamGen
Trained on 100,000+ hours of human-centric real-world interaction data with Day-0 adaptation for domestic GPUs (MetaX, Biren, Hygon)
Forms a closed 'See-Think-Act' data loop with ACE Ambient Capture and Embodied Superbrain A1
applications: Physical commonsense learning & virtual robot training

specs.architecture: Unified multimodal understanding-generation-prediction + Puffin spatial perception
specs.modality: 3D spatial view perception, dynamic physical interaction & mechanics input
specs.horizon: Supports up to 7-minute long-horizon video generation & physics simulation
specs.action_conditioned: Supports direct mechanics input and static/dynamic object separation
specs.training_data: 100,000+ hours human-centric physical interaction data + millions of hours internet video
specs.use_case: Embodied physical simulation, virtual trial-and-error & commercial closed loop
specs.benchmark_note: #1 on WorldModelBench Robot (9.30), LIBERO-Plus (89.0), RoboTwin 2.0 (96.1%) & DreamGen; Day-0 domestic GPU support

hybridvla.description: HybridVLA from Peking University unifies continuous diffusion denoising and autoregressive reasoning inside a single LLM (7B & 2.7B). Pretrained on 760K trajectories across 35 datasets, it outperforms prior SOTA VLAs by 14% in simulation and 19% on real-robot tasks.
highlights: Unifies diffusion continuous actions and autoregressive reasoning inside one LLM
Collaborative action ensemble beats prior SOTA by 14% (sim) and 19% (real)
Pretrained on 760K robot trajectories (33M frames) across 35 open datasets
Open-source code and weights in both 7B and 2.7B sizes

specs.architecture: Collaborative diffusion denoising + autoregression inside a single LLM (7B / 2.7B)
specs.training_data: 760K trajectories (33M frames) from 35 open datasets + real-world fine-tuning
specs.embodiments: Single-arm and bimanual robot platforms
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; generalizes across unseen objects, backgrounds and lighting
specs.benchmark_note: +14% mean success in sim and +19% in real-world tasks over prior SOTA VLAs
specs.deploy_note: Open-source weights and code supporting single- and multi-view fine-tuning

opengalaxea-g05.description: Galaxea G0.5 from Galaxea AI is an open-source unified autoregressive VLA that emits embodied chain-of-thought reasoning and 27-DoF ActionCodec tokens in a single transformer stream, achieving SOTA across LIBERO (98.9%), RoboTwin 2.0 (93.3%), and real-world R1-Lite/Pro.
highlights: Shifts from VLM-as-Encoder to VLM-as-Actor with one unified autoregressive stream
27-DoF cross-embodiment ActionCodec reaches 76.7% on real R1-Lite/Pro (vs 53.3% π0.5)
SOTA across 7 regimes: LIBERO (98.9%), RoboTwin 2.0 (93.3%), BEHAVIOR-1K (31.4%), DROID (82.5%)
Fully open-sourced and integrated into Hugging Face LeRobot

specs.architecture: VLM-as-Actor single autoregressive stream (native CoT + action tokens)
specs.backbone: Qwen3 VLM backbone + factorized spatial-temporal visual memory
specs.training_data: Large-scale multi-embodiment robot datasets + VQA co-training
specs.embodiments: Galaxea R1-Lite / R1-Pro, Franka DROID, etc.
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; 27-DoF ActionCodec skips idle degrees of freedom
specs.benchmark_note: 98.9% LIBERO, 93.3% RoboTwin 2.0, 82.5% DROID zero-shot, 31.4% BEHAVIOR-1K
specs.deploy_note: Integrated into LeRobot; prompts steer action granularity without extra training

eo-1.description: EO-1 is an open-source 3B unified embodied foundation model initialized from Qwen2.5-VL. Trained on interleaved vision-text-action data with both next-token prediction and flow-matching objectives, it achieves strong multimodal reasoning and CALVIN control.
highlights: Lightweight 3B open unified embodied model initialized from Qwen2.5-VL
Interleaved vision-text-action pretraining bridges embodied reasoning and control
Single decoder-only transformer combining discrete LM head and continuous flow matching
Open-sourced and integrated into Hugging Face LeRobot

specs.architecture: Single decoder-only transformer (discrete LM head + continuous flow-matching head)
specs.training_data: Interleaved vision-text-action embodied pretraining corpus
specs.embodiments: Single-arm, bimanual and simulation benchmark platforms
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; interleaved pretraining aligns reasoning and acting
specs.benchmark_note: Leading performance on CALVIN and multimodal embodied reasoning benchmarks
specs.deploy_note: Compact 3B footprint integrated with LeRobot for accessible fine-tuning

lingbot-vla-2.description: LingBot-VLA 2.0 is Robbyant's (Ant Group) next-gen open-source VLA foundation model released in July 2026. Pairing a Qwen3-VL-4B backbone with a sparse MoE Qwen2 action expert (32 experts, top-4 routing) pretrained on 60,000 hours of data, it is integrated into Hugging Face LeRobot as lingbot_vla_v2.
highlights: Scales pretraining to 60,000 hours of curated data including 50,000 hours of real robot trajectories
Qwen3-VL-4B backbone paired with a sparse MoE Qwen2 action expert (32 experts, top-4 routing)
Uses Flow Matching over a 55-D canonical shared state/action space with dual-query depth & video distillation
Fully open-sourced code and weights, integrated into Hugging Face LeRobot (lingbot_vla_v2)

specs.architecture: Qwen3-VL-4B backbone + sparse MoE Qwen2 action expert (32 experts, top-4 routing)
specs.action_head: Flow Matching continuous action chunks (55-D canonical shared space)
specs.training_data: 60,000 hours curated pretraining data (including 50,000 hours real robot data)
specs.embodiments: Single-arm, dual-arm and mobile manipulation platforms
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; 55-D canonical shared space + dual-query depth/video distillation
specs.benchmark_note: Substantial gains over LingBot-VLA v1 and concurrent open-source baselines across sim & real tasks
specs.deploy_note: Integrated into Hugging Face LeRobot as lingbot_vla_v2 for accessible fine-tuning

lingbot-world.description: LingBot-World is Robbyant's open-source interactive video world model (arXiv:2601.20540) supporting versatile physical interactions and fast generation, expanding into lingbot-world-fast and the interactive lingbot-world-v2.
highlights: Open-source interactive video world model from Robbyant, alongside fast and v2 variants
Supports versatile action/viewpoint interactions with long-horizon spatial consistency
Open weights and inference code available on GitHub and ModelScope
Pairs with LingBot-VLA in Robbyant's embodied foundation model stack
applications: Offline robot policy evaluation & data synthesis

specs.architecture: Open-source real-time interactive video world model (fast & v2 variants)
specs.modality: Interactive 3D scene & physical dynamics video generation
specs.action_conditioned: Supports versatile action and viewpoint conditioning
specs.training_data: Large-scale physical world & interactive video data
specs.use_case: Interactive embodied simulation, fast generation & policy evaluation
specs.benchmark_note: Includes high-speed lingbot-world-fast and interactive lingbot-world-v2 releases

lingbot-touch.description: LingBot-Touch is an open-source generalist tactile foundation model released by Robbyant in Nov 2026. By encoding contact-rich signals into plug-and-play tactile tokens, it boosts mean success across Diffusion Policy, π0.5, LingBot-VLA, and T-Rex by 13.9+ percentage points across 26 real-robot dexterous hand tasks.
highlights: Open-source generalist tactile foundation model released by Robbyant in November 2026
Outputs plug-and-play tactile tokens compatible with mainstream VLA and imitation policies
Raises mean success across Diffusion Policy, π0.5, LingBot-VLA, and T-Rex by 13.9+ pts on 26 dexterous hand tasks
Bridges vision-only policy blind spots in occluded grasping and contact-rich manipulation
applications: Industrial insertion, assembly & deformable object handling

specs.architecture: Generalist tactile representation & control foundation model for dexterous hands
specs.backbone: Generalist tactile encoder & multimodal alignment module
specs.action_head: Plug-and-play tactile tokens injected into downstream VLAs
specs.training_data: Cross-hand contact-rich real-robot tactile manipulation data
specs.embodiments: Compatible with multiple high-DOF dexterous hands
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; plugs into Diffusion Policy, π0.5, LingBot-VLA & T-Rex
specs.benchmark_note: +13.9+ percentage points mean success across 26 real-robot tasks on two dexterous hands
specs.deploy_note: Lightweight tactile-token interface for existing VLA policies

ace-ego.description: ACE-Ego is a human-centric embodied pretraining framework and model released by ACE Robotics in June 2026. Using dual-level reliability-adaptive objectives (full-weight robot sensor supervision + 3-tier filtered human video action reconstruction), it unifies VLA and WAM to bridge retail toward flexible industrial manufacturing.
highlights: Core pretraining framework of ACE Robotics' human-centric ACE paradigm
Dual-level reliability-adaptive objectives: full-weight robot supervision + 3-tier filtered human video action reconstruction
Unifies Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Model (WAM) capabilities
Accelerates transfer from commercial retail toward industrial and flexible manufacturing
applications: First-person human video to robot skill transfer

specs.architecture: Human-centric embodied pretraining framework unifying VLA and WAM
specs.backbone: ACE unified representation backbone (vision, egocentric action & world dynamics)
specs.training_data: Large-scale egocentric human video (Ambient Capture) + real robot sensor data
specs.embodiments: Cross-embodiment retail & flexible manufacturing robots
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; unified egocentric representation bridges human demos and robot bodies
specs.benchmark_note: Fuses VLA generalization with WAM dynamics prediction for industrial expansion
specs.deploy_note: Co-operates with ACE Ambient Capture and Kairos world model

graspvla.description: GraspVLA (CoRL 2025) from Peking University (EPIC Lab) and Galbot is a billion-frame grasp VLA foundation model trained entirely on 1B synthetic grasp frames (SynGrasp-1B) co-trained with internet image-text data, combining autoregressive perception CoT with flow-matching action generation for zero-shot sim-to-real grasping.
highlights: First grasp VLA foundation model pretrained entirely on billion-scale synthetic action data (SynGrasp-1B)
Progressive Action Generation bridges autoregressive 2D/3D bbox & grasp-pose perception with flow-matching actions
Achieves 90%+ zero-shot real-world open-vocabulary grasping across transparent, reflective and cluttered objects
Open-sources pretrained weights, evaluation code and the 1B-frame SynGrasp-1B dataset

specs.architecture: Progressive Action Generation (CoT): autoregressive perception (2D/3D boxes & grasp pose) + Flow Matching actions
specs.backbone: Multimodal VLM backbone + spatially grounded CoT intermediate representation
specs.training_data: 1 billion frames of synthetic grasp action data (SynGrasp-1B) co-trained with internet vision-language data
specs.embodiments: Single-arm and dual-arm manipulators across varied camera views
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; direct zero-shot sim-to-real transfer plus few-shot human preference post-training
specs.benchmark_note: 90%+ real-world success on transparent/cluttered/long-tail objects (accepted at CoRL 2025)
specs.deploy_note: Open-sources both SynGrasp-1B dataset and pretrained model checkpoints

crossformer.description: CrossFormer from UC Berkeley (RAIL) and CMU is a scalable 130M-parameter cross-embodiment transformer policy trained on 900,000 trajectories across 20–30 robots, controlling single/dual arms, wheeled navigators, quadrupeds (Go1), and quadcopters with the same shared weights.
highlights: Single 130M-parameter policy controls single/dual arms, Unitree Go1 quadrupeds, wheeled bases, and quadcopters
Requires no manual alignment of observation spaces, action dimensions, or control frequencies
Trained on 900K trajectories across ~30 robots, reaching 73% mean real-robot success (beating 67% single-robot specialists)
Fully open-source MIT code and 130M pretrained checkpoint
applications: Unified policy across arms, quadrupeds & drones

specs.architecture: Scalable cross-embodiment Transformer policy (no manual observation/action alignment)
specs.backbone: ResNet-26 visual encoders + variable-length multimodal sequence Transformer
specs.action_head: Multi-embodiment continuous readout heads (arms, bimanual, quadruped, navigation, quadcopter)
specs.training_data: 900,000 trajectories across 20–30 heterogeneous robot embodiments
specs.embodiments: Franka/WidowX arms, ALOHA bimanual, Unitree Go1 quadruped, wheeled robots & quadcopters
specs.cross_embodiment: Very strong; single shared network weights control manipulation, locomotion, navigation & flight
specs.benchmark_note: 73% mean success across 6 diverse real robots (vs 67% specialist policies and 51% prior cross-embodiment SOTA)
specs.deploy_note: Compact 130M footprint runs at each robot's native control frequency on consumer GPUs

cogact.description: CogACT from Microsoft Research is a componentized VLA architecture (~7.7B) that decouples VLM cognition from continuous action generation via a specialized Diffusion Action Transformer (DiT) and Adaptive Action Ensemble, outperforming 7B OpenVLA by >35% and beating 55B RT-2-X.
highlights: Decouples VLM cognition from continuous control using a specialized Diffusion Action Transformer (DiT)
Introduces Adaptive Action Ensemble (AAE) to smoothly aggregate multi-step action chunks
Outperforms 7B OpenVLA by >35 percentage points and beats 55B RT-2-X in simulation and real-robot evaluations
Open-sources Small, Base, and Large DiT action checkpoints and code under the MIT license

specs.architecture: Componentized VLM cognition backbone + conditioned Diffusion Action Transformer (DiT)
specs.action_head: Conditioned Diffusion Action Transformer (DiT-Small/Base/Large) + Adaptive Action Ensemble (AAE)
specs.training_data: Open X-Embodiment large-scale multi-robot trajectories
specs.embodiments: Google Robot, WidowX, Franka, bimanual and tabletop arms
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; rapid few-shot adaptation to new embodiments and unseen objects
specs.benchmark_note: Beats 7B OpenVLA by >35% mean success and surpasses 55B RT-2-X on SIMPLER & real arms
specs.deploy_note: MIT open-source weights available with DiT-Small, DiT-Base, and DiT-Large action modules

spatialvla.description: SpatialVLA from Shanghai AI Lab is an open-source 4B spatially enhanced VLA model pretrained on 1.1 million real-robot episodes, introducing calibration-free Ego3D Position Encoding and Adaptive Action Grids for strong 3D zero-shot and fine-tuned manipulation.
highlights: Introduces calibration-free Ego3D Position Encoding to inject 3D spatial context into a 2D VLM
Proposes Adaptive Action Grids to discretize continuous 3D actions into transferable spatial action tokens
Pretrained on 1.1 million real-world robot episodes for strong zero-shot cross-view robustness
Lightweight 4B footprint with MIT-licensed code and Hugging Face checkpoints (spatialvla-4b-224-pt)

specs.architecture: Spatially enhanced VLA: Ego3D Position Encoding + Adaptive Action Grids
specs.training_data: 1.1 million real-robot manipulation episodes
specs.embodiments: Multiple single-arm and mobile manipulation platforms
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; camera-centric Ego3D and adaptive grids enable zero-shot & fast fine-tuning
specs.benchmark_note: Significantly outperforms OpenVLA and Octo across SIMPLER, LIBERO and real-robot evaluations
specs.deploy_note: 4B parameters; open checkpoints on Hugging Face (IPEC-COMMUNITY/spatialvla-4b-224-pt)

gemini-robotics-1-5.description: Gemini Robotics 1.5 & ER 1.5 (Sept 2025) from Google DeepMind form a dual-model embodied agentic system pairing the GR-ER 1.5 orchestrator VLM with the GR 1.5 Thinking VLA and cross-embodiment Motion Transfer, halving long-horizon failure rates to 22%.
highlights: Agentic dual-model loop: GR-ER 1.5 handles planning/tool use while GR 1.5 executes with natural-language internal thinking
Motion Transfer generalizes skills across heterogeneous embodiments (ALOHA, bi-arm Franka, Apptronik Apollo)
GR-ER 1.5 scores 59.6 ER avg across 15 academic benchmarks (80.7 MMMU, 83.3 GPQA)
Cuts long-horizon failure rate from 44.5% to 22% across 230 evaluation tasks

specs.architecture: Dual-model agentic system: GR-ER 1.5 VLM orchestrator + GR 1.5 Thinking VLA
specs.action_head: Thinking-augmented continuous action generation + Motion Transfer
specs.training_data: Large-scale multi-embodiment teleop + cross-embodiment motion transfer + web multimodal data
specs.embodiments: ALOHA, Bi-arm Franka, Apptronik Apollo humanoid
specs.cross_embodiment: Strong; transfers behaviors across heterogeneous morphologies
specs.benchmark_note: 59.6 ER score across 15 benchmarks; halves long-horizon failure rate from 44.5% to 22%
specs.deploy_note: Trained on TPU v4/v5p/v6e with JAX; closed-source commercial & partner deployment

internw0.description: InternW0 (Sept 2026) from Shanghai AI Laboratory is an asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) World Action Model coupling a Video-DiT with a lightweight Action-DiT via asynchronous duplex inference (60.73 ms / 16.47 Hz on RTX 5090D), achieving 98.6% on LIBERO and 93.12% on RoboTwin 2.0-Full.
highlights: Asymmetric MoT WAM with asynchronous duplex inference and layerwise chunk K/V editor
60.73 ms critical-path latency (16.47 Hz) on RTX 5090D—3.13x faster than Fast-WAM
98.6% on LIBERO, 93.12% on RoboTwin 2.0-Full, and #1 (75.60%) on Clean2Random
68.4% progress rate on real-world wet-lab MoF experiments and 65.3% on 20-DoF quantitative pipetting

specs.architecture: Asymmetric MoT WAM: Video-DiT (Wan VAE) + lightweight Action-DiT (DINOv3) with async duplex inference
specs.modality: Video world prediction + 37-D unified action/state + optional force/tactile post-training
specs.horizon: Asynchronous duplex closed-loop control with layerwise chunk K/V editor
specs.action_conditioned: Bidirectional Video-DiT and Action-DiT coupling with tactile/force post-training
specs.training_data: 7,233.5 hours (811,969 episodes) across 7 datasets (InternData-A1, AgiBotWorld, RoboCOIN, Galaxea, EgoLab, etc.)
specs.use_case: Real-time closed-loop world-action control and long-horizon dexterous manipulation
specs.benchmark_note: 16.47 Hz on RTX 5090D; LIBERO 98.6%, RoboTwin 2.0-Full 93.12%, Clean2Random 75.60% (#1)

diffusion-policy.description: Diffusion Policy (March 2023) from Columbia, Stanford, and TRI formulates visuomotor robot control as conditional denoising diffusion (DDPM) with receding-horizon action chunking, improving mean success by 46.9% across 15 tasks and founding the modern diffusion/flow VLA action head.
highlights: Pioneered conditional DDPM action generation for visuomotor robot policies
Naturally captures multimodal action distributions with stable training and receding-horizon control
46.9% average improvement across 15 tasks from 4 benchmarks; 95% on real-world Push-T
MIT open-source baseline underlying modern diffusion and flow-matching VLA action heads

specs.architecture: Conditional DDPM + receding-horizon action chunking (CNN FiLM / Diffusion Transformer)
specs.backbone: ResNet-18 vision encoder + 1D temporal U-Net or Diffusion Transformer
specs.action_head: DDPM / DDIM action-sequence denoising (100 train / 10–16 eval steps)
specs.training_data: Robomimic, Push-T, BlockPush, Franka Kitchen, and real single/bimanual teleop demos
specs.embodiments: UR5, Franka Panda single-arm and bimanual platforms
specs.cross_embodiment: Foundational single/multi-task paradigm inspiring modern VLA action heads
specs.benchmark_note: +46.9% average improvement across 15 tasks; 95% real Push-T and 90% Mug Flip
specs.deploy_note: 0.1 s latency on RTX 3080 via 10-step DDIM; classic MIT open-source baseline

specs.architecture: Video diffusion transformer + decoupled action expert (retains video co-training, skips test-time future generation)
specs.backbone: Pretrained video generation diffusion transformer (~6.02B trainable params)
specs.action_head: Flow-matching/diffusion action expert denoising directly on cached current-frame features
specs.training_data: LIBERO (500 demos/suite) & RoboTwin (2,500 clean + 25,000 domain-randomized demos)
specs.embodiments: Single-arm tabletop & RoboTwin bimanual simulation/real platforms
specs.cross_embodiment: Achieves SOTA-competitive manipulation without large-scale embodied pretraining
specs.benchmark_note: 97.6% mean across 4 LIBERO suites (Spatial 98.2%, Object 100%, Goal 97.0%, Long 95.2%) & 91.8% on RoboTwin without pretraining
specs.deploy_note: 190 ms real-time latency, >4× faster than imagine-then-execute WAMs (Fast-WAM-IDM at 810 ms)

highlights: Disentangles video co-training from test-time imagination, showing WAM gains mainly stem from training-time video supervision
Skips test-time future-frame generation to achieve 190 ms latency (>4× faster than imagine-then-execute baselines)
Hits 97.6% mean success on LIBERO and 91.8% on RoboTwin without embodied pretraining
Serves as the foundational open baseline for Light-WAM, Faster-WAM, and LoopedWAM
applications: Efficient World Action Model (WAM) training research
fast-wam.description: Fast-WAM (Tsinghua IIIS, March 2026) is a World Action Model (~6.02B params) that retains video co-training during training but skips test-time future generation, cutting latency to 190 ms (>4× faster) with 97.6% mean LIBERO success.

specs.architecture: Shared differentiable world model + analytic gradients (BPTT over short imagined rollouts) for whole-body control
specs.backbone: Unified differentiable dynamics world model fit from rigid-body simulator transitions (built on mjlab)
specs.action_head: Humanoid whole-body motion-tracking policy co-trained with the world model
specs.training_data: Large human motion datasets (1–264 hours of motion, covering 129,514 benchmark motions)
specs.embodiments: Unitree G1 and humanoid bipedal platforms
specs.cross_embodiment: Single policy amortized across all motions without per-motion specialist distillation
specs.benchmark_note: Surpasses 128-GPU 7-day baseline in 3 hours on 1 GPU (>1000× fewer GPU-hours); 25 failures vs. 179 on 129,514 motions, 0 failures in 9.8h on 2 GPUs
specs.deploy_note: Transfers directly to physical Unitree G1 for diverse and acrobatic whole-body motions

highlights: CoRL 2026 Oral & Best Paper Award winner, slashing humanoid motion-tracking compute by >1000×
Outperforms a 128-GPU 7-day baseline in just 3 hours on a single GPU
Cuts failures on 129,514 benchmark motions from 179 to 25 (and reaches 0 failures in 9.8 hours on 2 GPUs)
Open-source mjlab implementation with verified sim-to-real transfer on Unitree G1
applications: Whole-body humanoid motion tracking & acrobatic control
supermimic.description: SuperMimic (UC Berkeley, CoRL 2026 Best Paper Award) trains a unified humanoid whole-body motion-tracking policy using a shared differentiable world model, beating a 128-GPU 7-day baseline in 3 hours on a single GPU and transferring to Unitree G1.

mobilewam.orgZh: Tsinghua AIR / HKUST-GZ / SJTU / Li Auto

specs.architecture: Mixture-of-Transformers (30-block Wan video DiT + 3-expert Mobile MoE action expert) + training-only Chain-of-Foresight
specs.backbone: Pretrained 30-block Wan video diffusion transformer (width 3072) + frozen T5 & 3D VAE
specs.action_head: Width-1024 action expert with soft-routed shared/locomotion/manipulation MoE (20 flow-matching steps, 13-DoF chunks)
specs.training_data: ManiSkill-HAB (1,000 filtered demos/subtask) & real ARX Lift2 teleoperation demos
specs.embodiments: Fetch simulated mobile manipulator & real ARX Lift2 wheeled dual-arm robot
specs.cross_embodiment: RGB-only two-view (head + wrist) whole-body control without point clouds or privileged segmentation
specs.benchmark_note: 73.0% mean S.R. on ManiSkill-HAB SetTable (+17.4 pts over AC-DiT); 15% on longest real ARX Lift2 compound task (vs. 0% for π0.5)
specs.deploy_note: Drops video branch & CoF at inference for 938 ms latency on A800 (5.3× faster than Motus, 8.7× faster than LingBot-VA)

highlights: First systematic adaptation of video-generation World Action Models to whole-body mobile manipulation
Chain-of-Foresight (CoF) chains future-latent beliefs during training for causal consistency at zero inference cost
Three-expert Mobile MoE (shared, locomotion, manipulation) resolves destructive gradient interference
Achieves 73.0% SOTA on ManiSkill-HAB with RGB-only one-stage training and 5–8× speedup over generate-then-act WAMs
applications: Long-horizon wheeled humanoid & mobile bimanual household tasks
Coordinated base-arm navigation and manipulation under moving viewpoints
mobilewam.description: MobileWAM (~6.5B, Tsinghua AIR et al.) adapts video-generation World Action Models to whole-body mobile manipulation via a 3-expert Mobile MoE and zero-inference-cost Chain-of-Foresight, reaching 73.0% on ManiSkill-HAB and beating π0.5 on a real ARX Lift2.
